provenance.paper_title: VideoTree: Adaptive Tree-based Video Representation for LLM Reasoning on Long Videos

representation_paths.memory_component: query-adaptive hierarchical tree over video clusters, whose nodes hold a representative keyframe and its VLM caption

evidence.paraphrase: Frames are encoded with EVA-CLIP-8B and K-Means clustered; the frame nearest each centroid becomes the cluster keyframe and is captioned by a VLM; the LLM scores each cluster caption for query relevance on a 1-3 scale, and the cluster count k is doubled and the loop repeated until enough high-relevance information is present or a breadth cap is hit.

High-relevance first-level clusters are re-clustered into sub-clusters, giving the tree depth: 'somewhat relevant' clusters receive w sub-clusters and 'highly relevant' clusters receive a two-level subtree of branch width w, so keyframe budget is allocated hierarchically by relevance.

The tree is traversed to collect the selected node captions, which are re-ordered by their original timestamps and concatenated into a video description that is fed to the LLM for answering. Each caption stays tied to its source keyframe index, so the underlying frames remain recoverable from the node.

adjudication_notes: Borderline tier, resolved as T1. The tree is expanded iteratively using LLM relevance scores (Algorithm 1 lines 3-12), which superficially looks like an inference-time memory update. But the entire expansion loop is the formation of the memory artifact for a single query; once the tree is finalised it is only traversed and read to build the LLM prompt (lines 17-18), and it is not retained or reused for any later query. Under the guide's T1 clause, a structure built before downstream use and thereafter only queried remains T1, and query-conditioned construction does not raise the tier.

Frame embeddings from EVA-CLIP-8B are used for clustering and keyframe selection only; nothing latent is passed to downstream reasoning, so per the guide they do not constitute an independent latent representation path.
Training-free method: no learned or evolving memory policy exists at all, so T3 is not in question.
